title: Existence of a spanning tree
statement: Let $G$ be a connected simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$. Then there is a spanning subgraph $T$ of $G$ — a simple graph on the same vertex set $V$ with $T \le G$ — that is a tree, that is, $T$ is connected and contains no cycle.
hypotheses_covered: conclusion: exists T with T ≤ G (spanning subgraph) that is a tree
replaced: \emph{Every connected graph contains a spanning tree.}
